name: Nahali-Baglani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page naha1261 and reference record 552859 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference at all for nlx; only Masica 1993 (overview list), Grierson 1907, Watters 2013 (subclassification comment p. 9) and Zide 1966 (= Kuiper 1966 'Sources of the Nahali vocabulary', which is about the Nihali isolate nll, not this language). Note hh.bib tags: Grierson IX(III) 'Baglani or Nahar = Nahari-Baglani [nlx]'; Masica 1993 'Nahari-Baglani dialect of Bhili in N Nasik Dt'; Watters 2013 'Toranmal Nahali = Nahali [nlx]'.

sources.citation: Shodhganga (INFLIBNET) Indian thesis repository, searches 'Nahali', 'Kalto', 'Nandurbar Bhil language phonology'
sources.note: No thesis on Nahali/Kalto Bhil; hits are Chaman Nahal literary studies and Bhil ethnography/economics theses.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives search for language code nlx (the Internet Archive copy, 2023)
sources.note: Only one SIL item exists for nlx: Watters 2013 (archive 52641). No phonology or grammar sketch.

sources.citation: Watters, Stephen. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Bhils of Northern Dhule District. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-004. Dallas: SIL International. vi+125 pp. (https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/52641)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexical-similarity (210-item wordlist) and recorded-text intelligibility survey; 'Toranmal Nahali' is treated as one of three Pauri dialects (with Bareli and Rathwi), pp. 15-17; pp. 4-5 note the Nahals of Toranmal 'speak a language similar to Pauri' and another 'Nahale' community near Amalwadi speaks something like Ahirani. No stress/accent/suprasegmental remark anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group, Part III: The Bhil Languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Bāglāṇī or Nahārī' section, p. 148 (No. 48-49 specimens).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. One introductory paragraph (location in Baglan/Satana/Malegaon/Kalwan/Pimpalner, etymology 'river-language', census figures, 'does not differ much from Khandesi', a few verb forms) followed by two specimens supplied by A. H. A. Simcox (1899). No remark on accent, stress or pronunciation for this dialect.

sources.citation: Any descriptive sketch of Pauri Bareli [bfb, paur1240] / Rathwi Bareli [bgd] with a phonology section (e.g. SIL or Indian-university wordlist/phonology reports on Pauri/Barela of Nandurbar-Barwani)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Watters 2013 shows Toranmal Nahali is a Pauri dialect (96% intelligibility, lexical similarity in the 65-73% band with Bareli/Rathwi); a Pauri stress statement is the nearest proxy.

sources.citation: Phillips, Maxwell P. 2012. Dialect continuum in the Bhil tribal belt: grammatical aspects. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: Most recent comparative grammatical treatment of the Bhil varieties surrounding Nahali (Pauri/Bareli, Rathwi, Noiri, Khandeshi); may contain a phonological sketch with word-stress remarks for the Pauri group to which Watters assigns Toranmal Nahali. Whether it covers Nahali by name is unverified (SOAS eprints could not be reached by automated download: DNS failure).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1907. LSI Vol. IX Part III, pp. 1-14 (introductory remarks on Bhili as a whole) and pp. 157-174 (Bhil dialects of the Satpudas / Khandesh, incl. Pauri and Kotali).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy downloaded when we checked the sources
sources.note: Already held by the project (no text layer; scanned djvu text held). The general Bhili introduction and the Khandesh/Satpuda sections were not read page by page for an accent remark that might be stated for Bhili as a whole and apply by inheritance to Baglani; a targeted read of pp. 1-14 and 157-174 is the one cheap remaining check.

sources.citation: Masica, Colin P. 1993. The Indo-Aryan languages. Cambridge: CUP. (Glottolog overview ref; lists 'Nahari-Baglani dialect of Bhili in N Nasik Dt-Maharashtra' in its dialect appendix per hh.bib language code field)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Not opened. A pan-Indo-Aryan handbook; per the Glottolog/hh.bib record it only names Nahari-Baglani in a dialect list; would not contain a Nahali-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Kuiper, F. B. J. 1962. Nahali: A Comparative Study. Amsterdam: Noord-Hollandsche; Kuiper 1966. The sources of the Nahali vocabulary. In N. Zide (ed.), Studies in Comparative Austroasiatic Linguistics, 57-81. The Hague: Mouton.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Not opened; both concern the Nihali language isolate [nll, niha1238] of Nimar/Buldhana, not Indo-Aryan Nahali-Baglani [nlx]. Glottolog's attachment of Zide 1966 to naha1261 is a name confusion.
